chunks: Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Marwani said: Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Sulayman said in Faris that Muhammad ibn Yahya said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Rawasi said: Ja'far ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Yazid al-Rishk, on the authority of Matraf ibn Abd Allah, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn that The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) sent a group for battle and appointed Ali (peace be upon him) as its head. When they returned, he enquired about the mission. Hence, they answered: “Everything went well, except that he recited (the chapter): Say: He, Allah is One, in every prayer he led.” He asked: “O Ali, why did you do that?” Consequently, he answered: “Out of love for the chapter: Say: He, Allah is One.” The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) then said: “You only loved it, because Allah, the Mighty and High, loved you.”

key_terms.سَرِيَّةٌ: A small military expedition or raid led by a companion of the Prophet.
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and High (an honorific title for Allah).
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: The title of Surah Al-Ikhlas (Chapter 112 of the Quran), meaning 'Say: He, Allah is One'.
key_terms.لِحُبِّي: Out of my love / due to my love.

ai.seo_question: Why did Ali ibn Abi Talib recite Surah Al-Ikhlas in every prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* highlights the spiritual merit of Surah Al-Ikhlas by linking Ali ibn Abi Talib’s devotion to it with divine affection. The Prophet’s response, 'I loved it so that Allah would love you,' underscores the theological principle that love for the attributes of God (manifested in the Surah) elicits God's love, a key concept in Shia piety and the doctrine of *Wala'*. This incident serves as both a practical endorsement of the Surah’s recitation and a spiritual validation of Ali’s status.
